node_types.name: Service
node_types.definition: Deployable runtime component (process, server, browser app) that exposes endpoints, calls other services, or interfaces with channels

node_types.name: Endpoint
node_types.definition: REST API endpoint exposed by a service; receives a request and routes to an internal module

node_types.name: Store
node_types.definition: Persistent data store (SQLite, file system) that modules read from and write to

node_types.name: Module
node_types.definition: Internal logic unit inside a service; performs encode/decode/validation/persistence work, not directly addressable from outside

node_types.name: Format
node_types.definition: Wire format contract describing the byte-level structure of data exchanged between services or persisted to channels

node_types.name: Channel
node_types.definition: External interface to the user's environment (file download/upload, clipboard, network) that a service emits to or ingests from

node_types.name: Concern
node_types.definition: A category of stakeholder concern that the architecture must address (e.g. data integrity, portability, usability, performance); used to classify which runtime nodes serve which concerns

nodes.definition: Svelte SPA running in the browser; provides the animation editor and library UI; calls backend REST endpoints; emits to and ingests from file and clipboard channels
Go HTTP server on port 9080 using ogen-generated handlers from spec.yml; exposes REST endpoints for animation export and import
SQLite database with the saved_animations table holding name, dimensions, and frames_json for each saved animation
GET /api/animations/{id}/export returning the saved animation serialized as Sparse JSON in the response body

POST /api/animations/import accepting a Sparse JSON payload plus an optional conflict-resolution mode (rename | overwrite | cancel; default rename-with-suffix). Routes the payload through the validator before any persistence; on validation failure returns a 4xx response with field-specific actionable errors and leaves the library untouched.

Encode/decode logic between the internal saved-animation representation and the Sparse JSON wire format. On import: decodes a validated payload, applies the conflict-resolution mode (rename-with-suffix by default; overwrite or cancel if explicitly requested) when persisting via the store. On export: reads a saved animation and produces a versioned Sparse JSON document. Does not perform schema validation — trusts that incoming payloads have already cleared the validator.

Sparse JSON wire format with shape {version, name, width, height, frames:[[{x,y,c}, ...], ...]} where c is a 24-bit RGB integer and only non-black pixels are stored. The version field follows semver: same major guarantees forward-compatibility (older readers ignore unknown optional fields); a different major may be rejected by older decoders. Self-describing: name and dimensions travel with the data.
Browser file download (export) and file picker upload (import) for .json files containing Sparse JSON
Browser clipboard read/write for copy-paste sharing of Sparse JSON animation text

Input-validation gate for the import path: bounds payload size, validates JSON structure against the format_sparse schema, checks pixel coordinates against declared dimensions and color values within 0..0xFFFFFF; tolerates unknown optional fields within a known major format version; rejects with field-specific 4xx errors before any persistence work
Imported animations don't corrupt the library; round-trip is exact; persistence is transactional
Animation files travel across users, devices, and time without losing meaning; format is self-describing and versioned
Users can share and import animations through familiar channels (file, clipboard) without manually editing JSON or interpreting opaque errors
Files are small enough to share over mundane channels; encode/decode is fast enough for interactive UI

requirements.description: Users can export any saved animation as a file from the library UI
Users can import a Sparse JSON file into their animation library via the library UI
Wire format is the chosen Sparse JSON encoding (selected after benchmark study)
Exported file carries name, matrix dimensions and frame data without requiring external context to interpret
Export-then-import yields an animation with identical frames, name and dimensions to the original
Malformed, oversized or off-spec import payloads are rejected with clear error and library remains untouched
Export and import are declared in spec.yml (OpenAPI 3.1) and the backend handlers are ogen-generated
Users can copy a Sparse JSON animation to clipboard and paste one to import, without saving a file
Import payload has a hard byte-size cap; oversize requests are rejected before parsing
Imports are strictly validated against the format_sparse schema (required fields, types, structure) before any persistence work
Pixel coordinates are checked against declared width/height; color values are checked against the 0..0xFFFFFF range; out-of-range entries reject the import
Validation failures return a 4xx response identifying the specific field and reason, never leaking server-internal details
Import detects an existing animation with the same name before committing the write
Import API accepts a conflict-resolution mode of rename, overwrite, or cancel and behaves accordingly when a name collision is detected
When no resolution mode is specified, the default behavior on collision is rename-with-suffix; existing animations are never silently overwritten
format_sparse includes a version field stamped by the exporter on every produced file
Decoder rejects files whose major format version is unknown to it, with a clear error identifying the version mismatch
Decoder tolerates and ignores unknown optional fields within a known major version; new fields must be additive and non-load-bearing for older readers

satisfactions.explanation: export_endpoint exists, routes to codec which reads db and serializes to format_sparse
import_endpoint exists, routes to codec which decodes format_sparse and writes db
format_sparse node defines Sparse JSON encoding chosen by benchmark; codec uses it for both directions
format_sparse shape {name, width, height, frames} carries all context needed to reconstruct an animation without external metadata
codec encode and decode are inverses by construction over the format_sparse fields (name, width, height, every non-black pixel coord); black pixels reconstructed as default fill
backend node is defined as ogen-generated from spec.yml; new endpoints will be declared there and regenerated via 'mise run gen'
clipboard_channel exists; frontend emits_to and ingests_from it, sending/receiving Sparse JSON text
validator module added on import path; rejects malformed/oversized/off-spec payloads with field-specific 4xx errors before any persistence; library remains untouched on validation failure
validator enforces payload byte-size cap defined by spec.yml maxLength constraint on the request body; oversize requests rejected before parsing
validator validates against format_sparse schema using ogen-generated request types (required fields, structure, types) before codec is invoked
validator checks every pixel against declared width/height and color values within 0..0xFFFFFF; out-of-range entries reject the entire import
validator returns 4xx with structured error body identifying the specific field path and reason (e.g. frames[3].pixels[7].x out of range), no internal details leaked
codec checks the saved_animations table for an existing name in the same transaction as the insert, before commit
import_endpoint accepts a mode parameter (rename | overwrite | cancel) declared in spec.yml; codec branches behavior on the value
default mode when not specified is rename-with-suffix per import_endpoint definition; existing animations are never silently overwritten
format_sparse definition now includes version as a required field; codec stamps version on every export
codec inspects the version field and rejects unknown major versions with a clear error identifying the version mismatch
codec/validator tolerate and ignore unknown optional fields when the major version matches; new fields must be additive within a major
